y1: A vineyard owner went to the marketplace early in the morning and called workers. The daily wage was one denarius.
y2: The owner went out at nine o'clock, twelve o'clock, three o'clock, and even at five o'clock, one hour before sunset, and called people standing around without work.
y4: In the evening, the owner gave the wages, starting from the last ones to arrive. Even the one who worked for one hour got a denarius! Those who worked since morning thought they would get more, but they also got one denarius.
y5: When they grumbled, the owner said: “I kept my word. Are you upset because I am generous?” God is equally generous to those who come late.
y7: The mother of James and John came and asked: “Let my two sons sit in Your Kingdom, one on Your right and one on Your left.” The other disciples were angry.
y8: Jesus said: “Whoever wants to be great among you must be a servant to others. I also did not come to be served, but to serve and to give my life for many.”
y9: Two men whose eyes were opened
y10: Two blind men sitting by the road in Jericho shouted: “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!” Even though the people told them to be quiet, they shouted even louder.
y11: Jesus stopped and asked: “What do you want me to do for you?” “Let our eyes be opened.” Jesus had compassion, touched their eyes, and immediately they saw and followed Him.
verse: “Even as the Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
prayer: Jesus, I thank You that You came not to be served, but to serve and give Your life for me. Let me rejoice in the grace of God, who is generous even to those who come late. Let me be a person who loves the place of service more than a high place. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: vineyard. A field where grapevines are planted and grown. The vineyard owner called the workers.
d1: denarius. A silver coin that was one day's wage at that time. Everyone got one denarius.
d2: generous. Being good and giving freely. Are you upset because I am generous?
d3: servant. A person who helps and works for others. A great person is a servant.
d4: blind. A person whose eyes cannot see. Two blind men called Jesus.
